clues.why: A colony is a big family of insects; the stinging colony at the south-west edge lives in the beehives.

clues.text: The fodder for the winter is heaped high on wheels at the east edge. Fetch a bundle for the pony.
clues.redirect: There is no hay here. Which words in the clue tell you the most?
clues.why: Fodder is animal food such as hay; the hay heaped on wheels at the east edge is the hay cart.

clues.text: Old Bram's crank squeaks as the pail rises from the cold, dark depths. Bring him some grease.
clues.redirect: Old Bram does not fill pails here. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

redirects.object:water-trough: This trough is for the animals. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

clues.why: A pail cranked up from the depths by Old Bram comes from the well.

clues.text: Tessa's grinding stones have worn smooth. Take her a chisel so the baker's flour stays fine.
clues.redirect: No grain is ground into flour here. Read the clue again.
clues.why: Grinding stones that make the baker's flour turn at the mill, where Miller Tessa works.

clues.text: Storms washed the stepping stones away, but Aldo's crossing over the river still stands firm. Go there.
clues.redirect: This does not take you over the river. Which words in the clue tell you the most?
clues.why: Carpenter Aldo's crossing over the river, firm in any weather, is the bridge.

clues.text: Sister Wren polishes the bronze bell until it gleams, then waits for the hour to ring it. Go and keep her company.
clues.redirect: This is not where the bell rings. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.
clues.why: Sister Wren and her bell are at the chapel.

clues.text: Crier Pip calls out the price of apples to a jostling crowd of shoppers. Join them.
clues.redirect: There are no stalls here. Read the clue again.
clues.why: Jostling means pushing and crowding; Crier Pip calls prices to shoppers at the market.

clues.text: Hesper lends books, but she insists that each one comes back to the same shelf, safe and dry.
clues.redirect: There are no shelves of books here. Which words in the clue tell you the most?

redirects.object:notice-board: Signs are pinned up on this. Which words in the clue tell you the most?

clues.why: Hesper keeps the library's books shelved and safe.

clues.text: At dusk, the lantern high above the rooftops flickers to life. Mason Gerd begins his vigil over the hills.
clues.redirect: No lantern looks out over the hills from here. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

redirects.landmark:puzzle-tower: This tall place is full of puzzles. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

clues.why: A vigil is a night of keeping watch; Mason Gerd keeps it with his lantern at the watchtower.

clues.text: A bench sits in a patch of sunshine, surrounded by beds of savoury herbs. Ivy tends them all. Go there.
clues.redirect: No herbs grow here. Read the clue again.

redirects.object:beehives: These hives are homes for buzzing workers. Read the clue again.

clues.why: A sunny bench among herbs, tended by Keeper Ivy, is in the garden.

clues.text: Riders heading for the keep go north along the road until it ends. There they pass inside. Go and wait for them.
clues.redirect: This is not where the road ends. Which words in the clue tell you the most?
clues.why: The way into the castle, at the north end of the road, is the castle gate.

clues.text: Lost: one grey kitten. A sheet pinned up by the southern way into the village asks everyone to search their sheds.
clues.redirect: No signs are pinned up here. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

redirects.landmark:library: This is where Hesper keeps her shelves of books. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

clues.why: Sheets about lost things are pinned up at the notice board, by the southern entrance.

clues.text: The tolling begins at dusk, slow and steady. Sister Wren lights a candle as the village falls silent.
clues.redirect: This is not where the bell rings. Read the clue again.
clues.why: Tolling is the slow ringing of a bell; the bell and Sister Wren are at the chapel.

clues.text: Before the baker can knead a single loaf, golden kernels must be crushed into a fine white powder. Go where that happens.
clues.redirect: No grain is ground into flour here. Which words in the clue tell you the most?
clues.why: Kernels crushed into fine white powder become flour, and flour is made at the mill.

clues.text: Generations of villagers have lowered pails into the same deep shaft. Today, Old Bram is the one who tends it.
clues.redirect: Old Bram does not fill pails here. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

redirects.object:water-trough: This trough is for the animals. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

clues.why: A deep shaft that pails are lowered into, tended by Old Bram, is the well.

clues.text: The river once cut the village in two. Now sturdy timbers span the current, and Aldo makes sure they hold in every storm.
clues.redirect: This does not take you over the river. Read the clue again.
clues.why: Timbers that span the river and hold in every storm are the bridge, kept by Carpenter Aldo.

clues.text: Merchants display their wares beneath striped awnings, and a crier's voice rises above the bustle.
clues.redirect: There are no stalls here. Which words in the clue tell you the most?
clues.why: Wares are goods for sale and awnings are cloth roofs over stalls; a crier calls out at the market.

clues.text: Knowledge from every corner of the realm is shelved and kept safe from damp. Hesper is its guardian.
clues.redirect: There are no shelves of books here. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

redirects.object:notice-board: Signs are pinned up on this. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

clues.why: Knowledge kept on shelves, guarded by Hesper, is the library.

clues.text: Raiders could creep over the hills at night. Who would spot them first? The one who keeps the lantern burning up high.
clues.redirect: No lantern looks out over the hills from here. Read the clue again.

redirects.landmark:puzzle-tower: This tall place is full of puzzles. Read the clue again.

clues.why: The watchtower keeps eyes on the hills and a lantern at night.

clues.text: Ivy says a pinch of rosemary cures any dull stew. Gather some where the fragrant beds bask in the sun.
clues.redirect: No herbs grow here. Which words in the clue tell you the most?

redirects.object:beehives: These hives are homes for buzzing workers. Which words in the clue tell you the most?

clues.why: Rosemary is an herb, and Keeper Ivy's herb beds lie in the sun in the garden.

clues.text: Each dawn the keep admits its visitors at the north end of the road. To admit someone is to let them in. Go where they are admitted.
clues.redirect: This is not where the road ends. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.
clues.why: To admit is to let in; the castle lets visitors in at the north end of the road, at the castle gate.

clues.text: The day's quests are done, yet your mind still itches for a challenge. Seek the tall stone place at the south-east edge.
clues.redirect: There are no bonus puzzles here. Read the clue again.

redirects.landmark:watchtower: This is Mason Gerd's lookout over the hills. Read the clue again.

clues.why: A challenge for your mind means a puzzle, and the bonus puzzles wait in the Puzzle Tower at the south-east edge.

clues.text: Lost goats, harvest feasts, new babies. Every announcement ends up tacked by the southern way into the village.
clues.redirect: No signs are pinned up here. Which words in the clue tell you the most?

redirects.landmark:library: This is where Hesper keeps her shelves of books. Which words in the clue tell you the most?

clues.why: Announcements are tacked up at the notice board, beside the southern entrance.

clues.text: Muddy hoofprints lead to a long wooden basin at the south edge, where the village's beasts stop to slurp.
clues.redirect: This is not where the animals stop for a sip. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

redirects.landmark:well: Old Bram fills pails for the houses here. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

clues.why: Hoofprints lead animals to the long wooden basin at the south edge: the water trough.

clues.text: The colony at the south-west edge works from dawn to dusk. A careless visitor may earn a painful sting.
clues.redirect: No little wooden homes are here. Read the clue again.

redirects.landmark:garden: This is Keeper Ivy's place of herbs. Read the clue again.

clues.why: A stinging colony at the south-west edge lives in the beehives.

clues.text: A rickety wagon groans under its load of dried grass at the east edge. The farmer will need it for winter.
clues.redirect: There is no hay here. Which words in the clue tell you the most?
clues.why: Rickety means shaky; the wagon loaded with dried grass at the east edge is the hay cart.

clues.text: Every doorstep owes its full kettle to one deep shaft and the patient old man who winds its rope.
clues.redirect: Old Bram does not fill pails here. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

redirects.object:water-trough: This trough is for the animals. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

clues.why: A deep shaft with a rope, wound by Old Bram, fills every doorstep's kettle: the well.

clues.text: Grist goes in one end, and fine powder for the baker comes out the other. Tessa oversees it all, her hair dusted white.
clues.redirect: No grain is ground into flour here. Read the clue again.
clues.why: Grist is grain to be ground; turning it into flour for the baker happens at the mill.

clues.text: Aldo checks each plank that arches over the fast current. Thanks to him, no traveller gets wet feet.
clues.redirect: This does not take you over the river. Which words in the clue tell you the most?
clues.why: Timbers arching over the current, kept by Carpenter Aldo, are the bridge.

clues.text: Inside, the only sounds are soft footsteps and the creak of old pews. Above, a bell waits for Sister Wren's hand.
clues.redirect: This is not where the bell rings. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.
clues.why: Pews are long seats in a quiet place; the bell above and Sister Wren mean the chapel.

clues.text: Pip's voice carries over the clatter of crates and the chatter of buyers at the stalls.
clues.redirect: There are no stalls here. Read the clue again.
clues.why: Buyers at stalls, with Crier Pip calling out, are at the market.

clues.text: Hesper keeps a lamp burning low so no one squints at the pages. Every volume rests on its proper shelf.
clues.redirect: There are no shelves of books here. Which words in the clue tell you the most?

redirects.object:notice-board: Signs are pinned up on this. Which words in the clue tell you the most?

clues.why: Pages, volumes and shelves, kept by Hesper, mean the library.

clues.text: Gerd's post is lonely, but from up there he can see every road that winds over the hills.
clues.redirect: No lantern looks out over the hills from here. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

redirects.landmark:puzzle-tower: This tall place is full of puzzles. Think about what the clue's harder words mean.

clues.why: Mason Gerd's high post with a view of the hills is the watchtower.

clues.text: Ivy's bench catches the afternoon sun, and the air around it smells of thyme and lavender.
clues.redirect: No herbs grow here. Read the clue again.

redirects.object:beehives: These hives are homes for buzzing workers. Read the clue again.

clues.why: Thyme and lavender are herbs; Keeper Ivy's sunny bench is in the garden.

clues.text: After a long day of hauling, the oxen plod to the south edge. A long wooden basin waits for them there.
clues.redirect: This is not where the animals stop for a sip. Which words in the clue tell you the most?

redirects.landmark:well: Old Bram fills pails for the houses here. Which words in the clue tell you the most?

clues.why: The long wooden basin for animals at the south edge is the water trough.
